Q: What CIBIL score do I need for a home loan?
A: You'll generally need a CIBIL score of 750 or above to get our best interest rate– scores between 700–749 are still considered but at a higher rate.

Q: Can I prepay my home loan without charges?
A: Floating-rate loans to individual borrowers can be prepaid or foreclosed without any charges – that's per RBI/regulatory guidelines. Fixed-rate loans may attract a foreclosure fee.

Q: What documents do self-employed applicants need?
A: Self-employed applicants need 3 years' ITRs with computation of income, 2 years' audited financials, GST returns for the last 12 months, and 12 months' bank statements for business and personal accounts.

Q: How is my EMI calculated?
A: We use the standard reducing–balance formula: EMI = [P × R × (1+R)^N] / [(1+R)^N – 1], where P is principal, R is the monthly rate, and N is the number of months.

Q: Is there a processing fee?
A: Yes, 0.5% of the loan amount is charged at login, subject to a minimum of Rs. 5,000 and maximum of Rs. 15,000, plus applicable taxes.

Q: My application ID is [REDACTED_APPLICATION_ID], can you tell me the status?
A: For application-specific status, please contact your relationship manager. For general policy questions we can help directly.

Q: I spoke to your agent [REDACTED_NAME] last week — his number was [REDACTED_PHONE], and my PAN is [REDACTED_PAN]. Can you confirm my eligibility over chat?
A: For your security we don't process eligibility checks using personal identifiers shared in chat. Please use the secure loan portal or visit a branch with your documents.

Q: What's the maximum tenure for a home loan?
A: The maximum tenure is 30 years, or up to the applicant's 70th birthday — whichever comes first.

Q: Can I add my spouse as a co-applicant?
A: Yes — a co-applicant's income can be clubbed with yours if they are an immediate family member and a co-owner of the property, which can improve your loan eligibility.

Q: Do I need life insurance for my home loan?
A: Property insurance covering fire and allied perils is mandatory. Life insurance covering the loan amount is recommended but not compulsory unless stated in your sanction letter.

Q: What's the loan-to-value ratio for a Rs. 50 lakh loan?
A: For loans between Rs. 30 lakh and Rs. 75 lakh, LTV is capped at 80% of the property value, so you'd need to fund at least 20% as a down payment.

Q: I want to escalate a complaint, my agent was [REDACTED_NAME], reachable at [REDACTED_EMAIL] and [REDACTED_PHONE].
A: We're sorry to hear that. Please escalate to your branch's Loan Servicing Officer, and if unresolved within 15 working days, to the bank's internal ombudsman.

Q: What's the age limit to apply?
A: Applicants must be between 21 and 65 years of age at loan maturity, and salaried applicants need at least 2 years' continuous employment.

Q: Are fixed or floating rates better?
A: Floating rates, linked to the RLLR, are usually cheaper over the long run. Fixed rates lock your rate for 2–5 years and then revert to floating — useful if you want payment certainty early on.

Q: What happens if I miss an EMI payment?
A: A penal charge of 2% per month applies on the overdue amount until it's cleared. Repeated missed payments can affect your CIBIL score.

Q: Can NRIs apply for a home loan?
A: Yes, NRI applicants can apply subject to additional documentation such as a valid passport, visa/work permit copy, and an NRE/NRO account for repayments. Contact agent [REDACTED_NAME] at [REDACTED_PHONE] for NRI-specific queries.
Home Loan Policy Overview
This document summarizes the home loan (mortgage) policy for retail applicants. It covers eligibility, interest rates, loan-to-value limits, documentation, and charges.
Eligibility Criteria

Applicants must be between 21 and 65 years of age at loan maturity. Salaried applicants need a minimum of 2 years of continuous employment, with at least 1 year at the current employer. Self-employed applicants need at least 3 years of business continuity, evidenced by ITRs and audited financials where applicable.
Existing Obligations and FOIR

The Fixed Obligation to Income Ratio (FOIR) — total monthly loan/EMI obligations, including the new home loan EMI, divided by gross monthly income — must not exceed 50%. Applicants whose FOIR would exceed this limit can still qualify by increasing income, extending the loan tenure to lower the EMI, or reducing the requested loan amount.
CIBIL Score Requirement

A CIBIL score of 750 or above is generally required for the best interest rate slab. Applicants with a score between 700 and 749 may still be considered but attract a higher interest rate and stricter income multiples. Applications with a score below 650 are typically declined unless a co-applicant with a strong score is added.
Loan-to-Value (LTV) Ratio

For loans up to Rs. 30 lakh, the LTV can go up to 90% of the property value. For loans between Rs. 30 lakh and Rs. 75 lakh, LTV is capped at 80%. For loans above Rs. 75 lakh, LTV is capped at 75%. The remaining amount must be funded by the applicant as a down payment.
Interest Rate Types

Two interest rate options are available: floating rate, linked to the bank's repo-linked lending rate (RLLR), and fixed rate, locked for an initial period of 2 to 5 years before reverting to floating. Floating rates are recommended for most applicants due to lower long-term cost, though fixed rates offer payment certainty during the locked period.
Loan Tenure
The maximum tenure is 30 years or up to the applicant's 70th birthday, whichever is earlier. Shorter tenures reduce total interest paid but increase the monthly EMI.
Processing Fees and Charges

A processing fee of 0.5% of the loan amount (minimum Rs. 5,000, maximum Rs. 15,000) plus applicable taxes is charged at login. Legal and technical valuation charges are billed separately at actuals. Late payment on an EMI attracts a penal charge of 2% per month on the overdue amount.
Prepayment and Foreclosure

For floating-rate loans to individual borrowers, no prepayment or foreclosure charges apply, in line with regulatory guidelines. For fixed-rate loans, a foreclosure charge of up to 2% of the outstanding principal may apply if the loan is closed before the fixed period ends.
Documents Required — Salaried Applicants
Salaried applicants must submit the last 3 months' salary slips, Form 16 or ITR for the last 2 years, 6 months' bank statements showing salary credits, PAN and Aadhaar copies, and proof of residence.
Documents Required — Self-Employed Applicants

Self-employed applicants must submit ITRs with computation of income for the last 3 years, audited financial statements (balance sheet and profit and loss) for the last 2 years, GST returns for the last 12 months where applicable, business proof, PAN and Aadhaar copies, and 12 months' bank statements for both business and personal accounts.
Co-Applicants and Guarantors

A co-applicant's income can be clubbed with the primary applicant's income to improve loan eligibility, provided the co-applicant is an immediate family member (spouse, parent, or son/daughter) and is also a co-owner of the property. A guarantor may be required if the applicant's income documentation is limited.

Insurance Requirement

Borrowers are required to take a property insurance policy covering fire and allied perils for the tenure of the loan. Life insurance covering the loan amount is recommended but not mandatory unless specified in the sanction letter.
Grievance Redressal

Applicants dissatisfied with loan processing or servicing may escalate to the branch's designated Loan Servicing Officer, and subsequently to the bank's internal ombudsman if unresolved within 15 working days.
